title: The Daegu Shop Lee Byung-chul Opened After Losing His Masan Land
conflicts: Lee's age at founding differs (28, 29 or 'exactly 30'), so none is given. The origin of the 30,000 won differs (family gift per Lankov; what remained after debts per Maeil Shinmun), so only the sum is given. Gale's company history puts the rice mill in Taegu and the early trade in wool; it conflicts with all Korean sources and was not used. Building size (Maeil: four storeys; JoongAng: small store) is not described.
notes: The episode is told as Lee's restart after the 1936-37 Masan rice mill and land collapse, ending in the 1 March 1938 Daegu opening; the slate's dried fish and noodles are kept. Two of the five sources are Korean-language (Maeil Shinmun, Daegu's daily) and load but do not name the founder in Latin script; three English sources (Aju Business Daily, Korea JoongAng Daily, Korea Times/Lankov) name him. The land-on-bank-credit detail rests on Maeil Shinmun (two articles) with Aju independently confirming liquidation through speculation.
